 Democrat Abdul El-Sayed and former Republican Rep. Mike Rogers face off to replace retiring Democratic Sen. Gary Peters. El-Sayed has been endorsed by high-profile progressives, including Sen. Bernie Sanders. Meanwhile Rogers is looking for a comeback after losing a Senate race in 2024, and has been endorsed by President Donald Trump, though Republicans haven’t won a Senate race in the state since 1994.

 Inside the Election
 From the Decision Desk Election Day voter turnout in Detroit is surpassing turnout from the 2022 midterm elections. By 5 p.m. ET in 2022, Detroit had around 66,000 people vote on Election Day. Today, at 5 p.m. ET, Detroit had around 75,000 votes, per the Detroit City clerk. Polls close in Michigan at 8 p.m.
 6:49 PM ET 
 From the Decision Desk Elections are administered by towns and municipalities, and counting usually takes until early morning or even midday Wednesday. How quickly the winner of this competitive Senate race can be called depends upon the margin. For that, all eyes will be on Wayne County, home of Detroit.
